title: Refugees stay close
hook: At the end of 2025, about 65% of refugees lived in a country bordering their own.
notes: Refugees: UNHCR Refugee Population Statistics, end-year stocks to the end of 2025 (also published on HDX under CC BY-IGO). 'Refugees' here are refugees under UNHCR's mandate plus 'other people in need of international protection' (mostly Venezuelans in Latin America). Not included: asylum seekers, people displaced inside their own country, and about 6 million Palestine refugees under UNRWA's mandate. Flows show origin–asylum pairs of at least 5,000 people. A neighbour is a country with a shared land border on the map. In 2024 UNHCR stopped listing about 1.2 million Ukrainians in Russia, so Ukraine's share in neighbouring countries drops from 2024. This is a statistical coverage break, not evidence that those people left Russia (UNHCR Global Trends 2024, https://www.unhcr.org/sites/default/files/2025-06/global-trends-report-2024.pdf). UNHCR documents large-scale Afghan returns and deportations from Iran and Pakistan in its 2025 recap, https://data.unhcr.org/en/documents/details/121254. Per 1,000 residents uses UN World Population Prospects 2024 (2025 projected), for countries with over 1 million people. Deaths: IOM Missing Migrants Project, incidents 2014–2024 as published on HDX (CC BY-IGO), dead and missing combined; the counts are a minimum, because many deaths are never recorded. Country tooltip totals cover all origins and destinations; the selected-origin stock links are a separate filtered view.

scenes.title: 36 million refugees
scenes.text: At the end of 2025 about 36 million people lived as refugees outside their country. Five countries account for nearly two-thirds of them: Venezuela (6.5 million), Ukraine (5.2 million), Syria (4.9 million), Afghanistan (3.7 million) and Sudan (2.8 million). Press Play to see crises rise and fall.

captions.2000: About 12 million refugees; Afghanistan is the largest group.
captions.2015: Syria's war: 4.9 million Syrians have fled.
captions.2022: Russia's full invasion: Ukrainians become one of the largest groups.
captions.2025: Many Syrians return home after Assad's fall; Iran and Pakistan push out Afghans.

chart.title: Largest refugee groups, by country of origin

scenes.title: Where refugees live
scenes.text: Colombia hosts the most refugees (2.8 million, nearly all from Venezuela), followed by Germany (2.7 million), Türkiye (2.4 million, mostly Syrians), Uganda (1.9 million) and Iran (1.7 million). Apart from Germany, the biggest hosts sit right next to a crisis.

scenes.title: Two in three stay next door
scenes.text: About 65% of refugees live in a country that borders their own. For people from Sudan, South Sudan or the Central African Republic it is over 90%. Ukrainians are more widely spread across Europe: about 30% are recorded in neighbouring countries. UNHCR's removal of Russia's Ukraine count from 2024 also affects that comparison.

layers.title: Share of a country's refugees living in a neighbouring country

scenes.title: Five crises, five patterns
scenes.text: Pick a crisis to see where its refugees went. Tap a country on the map to see only its flows.

options.label: Syria
options.text: Syrians fled mostly to neighbours: 2.3 million live in Türkiye, 530,000 in Lebanon and 420,000 in Jordan. Germany (670,000) is the one large host far away.

options.label: Ukraine
options.text: Ukrainians spread across Europe: Germany hosts 1.2 million, Poland 970,000 and Czechia 390,000. UNHCR no longer counts the 1.2 million it listed in Russia until 2023.

options.label: Venezuela
options.text: Venezuelans moved along the Andes: 2.8 million live in Colombia, 1.1 million in Peru, 700,000 in Brazil and 660,000 in Chile.

options.label: Sudan
options.text: Since war broke out in 2023, Sudanese have fled mostly to neighbouring countries: 1.3 million to Chad, 570,000 to South Sudan and 550,000 to Libya.

options.label: Afghanistan
options.text: Iran (1.6 million) and Pakistan (1.3 million) host most Afghan refugees. Both expelled many in 2024–25, and the number of Afghan refugees fell from 6.4 million in 2023 to 3.7 million.

scenes.title: The heaviest load
scenes.text: Relative to their own size, the countries next to a crisis carry the most. Lebanon hosts about 92 refugees for every 1,000 residents, roughly one in eleven people. Chad hosts 72 and Colombia 53. Germany hosts 32, the United States about 1.

scenes.title: Deadly routes
scenes.text: Some people try to go further. Between 2014 and 2024 the IOM recorded about 73,000 migrants and refugees who died or went missing on the way. Every circle is a place where people died; the bright ones are the year shown. In 2024 alone the count reached about 8,900, the highest on record.

layers.title: Dead and missing migrants, up to the year shown

captions.2016: The deadliest year in the Mediterranean: about 5,200 dead and missing.

scenes.title: The deadliest sea
scenes.text: The Mediterranean is the deadliest crossing: about 31,000 people died or went missing there in 2014–2024, 24,500 of them on the central route from North Africa to Italy and Malta. Thousands more died crossing the Sahara on the way north, and over 5,000 on the Atlantic route to the Canary Islands.
